evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/price_map.rs:226 get_price_map is the handler for the PUBLIC, UNAUTHENTICATED GET /api/v1/price-map (mounted bare at main.rs:515 `.nest("/api/v1/price-map", routes::price_map::router())`, router() at price_map.rs:174 attaches no auth/throttle layer).

reality-server has NO global per-IP rate-limit layer: the only abuse control (state.inquiry_rate_limiters) is invoked INSIDE the anonymous inquiry (routes/inquiries.rs enforce_inquiry_rate_limit) and report (routes/reports.rs enforce_public_report_rate_limit) POST handlers. The main.rs layer stack (L521-575: DefaultBodyLimit, security_headers, TraceLayer, CorsLayer, host_tenant_middleware) adds no request-rate throttle. So the price-map GET is reachable unthrottled.

On every cache MISS it runs an expensive double-CTE aggregation over `listings` (price_map.rs:253-330): current_period + prior_period, each a full `AVG(CASE WHEN size_sqm>0 THEN price/size_sqm END) ... GROUP BY city` scan. The cache_key (price_map.rs:253-259) is `"{mode}:{time_window}:{property_type}:{city}"` and embeds the RAW free-text `query.city` (L258) — an attacker rotating `?city=a1`, `?city=a2`, ... forces a guaranteed cache miss every request, so each request re-runs both aggregations against the DB.

The BoundedCache (MAX_PRICE_MAP_CACHE_ENTRIES=10_000 with LRU/insertion-order eviction, price_map.rs:57/142) bounds only MEMORY under a distinct-key flood (the existing #3132 tests confirm the OOM guard). It does NOT throttle the per-miss DB aggregation, and the LRU eviction means a distinct-key flood also evicts all legitimately-cached aggregations, collapsing the hit rate and the 1h cache benefit for real visitors. Net effect: an unauthenticated single-IP caller can impose repeated expensive GROUP BY load on the shared public DB pool and bust the cache for everyone.

Fix vector: add a per-IP throttle to the price-map GET (reuse the existing TenantRateLimiterSet / client_ip_bucket primitive already used for inquiries/reports), and/or reduce cache-miss amplification by validating+canonicalising `city` (trim/lowercase/known-city allowlist) before it enters cache_key so arbitrary free-text can't mint unbounded distinct keys. Confidence medium: the absent throttle layer and per-miss aggregation are certain by static read; 'medium' (not high) because the DB cost per aggregation was not runtime-measured from this cloud runner.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/price_map.rs:230 `let mode = query.mode.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "sale".to_string());` — the `mode` query param is accepted with NO allowlist validation and bound directly as `transaction_type = $1` (L324 `.bind(&mode)`).

This is inconsistent with its own sibling param in the SAME handler: `time_window` IS validated against a closed match (price_map.rs:238-253) — `1m|3m|12m|5y` map to intervals and any other value returns `400 BAD_REQUEST` ('Unsupported time_window ...'). `mode` gets no such treatment, though the only meaningful DB values are the transaction_type enum (e.g. sale/rent).

Consequence: an arbitrary `?mode=foo` does NOT 400 — it silently matches zero rows, returns `200 OK` with an empty `districts: []`, echoes the bogus `mode` back in PriceMapResponse (price_map.rs:204-212 / response build), and is cached under cache_key `"foo:3m::"` (L253-259). A silent empty 200 for an unsupported enum value is a contract defect (clients can't distinguish 'no data for a valid filter' from 'invalid filter'), and it compounds the distinct-key cache-miss surface of the sibling finding.

Fix vector: validate `mode` against the transaction_type allowlist up-front and return 400 on unknown values, mirroring the existing `time_window` closed-match guard a few lines above. Low severity / contract-consistency. Confidence medium: the missing validation and the silent-empty-200 path are certain by static read.
